statement: Users can know the update frequency of a Dataset
Users can find whether any two qb:Observations in the same qb:DataSet share identical values for all dimensions.
Users can judge that dimensions with range skos:Concept must have an associated qb:codeList for a Dimension.
Users can know that when a dataset’s distribution is only accessible via a landing page, the landing page link SHOULD be duplicated as an accessURL on the distribution.
Users can know the publisher of a catalog.
Users can know the datasets included in a Catalog via dcat:dataset.
Users can know whether appropriate URI sets already exist for relevant dimensions
Users can know the contact point for a Dataset
Users can find the public list of patent disclosures maintained by W3C for deliverables of the Working Group.
Users can know that a downloadable distribution can be linked via dcat:downloadURL without defining a separate dcat:Distribution instance
Publishers can indicate whether an attribute is required for every observation; otherwise the attribute is optional.
Publishers can know that when a code list is already available as a SKOS ConceptScheme or can reasonably be made so, they should use SKOS rather than qb:HierarchicalCodeList.
Users can know the publisher of a dataset
Users can retrieve life expectancy values for each reference area from observations linked to a dataset.
Users can know whether each qb:Observation in a DataSet that uses a Measure dimension has a value for its specific qb:measureType.
Users can know which dimensions are required for each qb:Observation in a qb:DataSet.
Users can judge that dimension values within a dataset are unambiguously defined, when evaluating the dataset's metadata.
Users can know the homepage of a Catalog
Users can find the landing page URL for a dataset.
Users can know that every DataStructureDefinition must include at least one declared measure for a DataStructureDefinition.
Users can find slice definitions (qb:Slice) for a dataset to understand how observations are grouped.
Users can know that the property qb:componentRequired indicates whether a component property is required (true) or optional (false) in a Data Structure Definition
Users can know what dimensions (time period, region, sex) are available for query and their presentational order.
Users can know that slices are used to group uniform subsets of observations where one or more dimension values are fixed.
Users can know the temporal coverage of a dataset.
Users can know the rights of a Catalog
Users can know whether an observation linked to a slice has its dataset correctly set to the dataset that contains the slice.
Users can know that the concept link is optional unless the concept is expected to be reused.
Users can know the units (years) of the measured values for each observation.
Users can know the language(s) of a dataset
Users can know that a slice key lists the component properties (dimensions) that will be fixed in the slice.
Publishers can know that an attribute component must be marked as required and attached to the DataSet when its qb:componentRequired property is true.
Publishers can decide to use code lists for dimension values when the dimension is included as a componentProperty of a SliceKey.
Users can know the reference period (refPeriod) associated with a slice to filter observations by time.
Users can know the values of each dimension required to locate an observation for a Dataset observation.
Users can know the license of a Catalog
Users can know how licensing information is expressed for a distribution.
Users can know the size of a Distribution
Users can know the description of a Catalog

Users can judge whether a data interchange conforms to the Data Cube vocabulary by checking that RDF graphs are well‑formed or well‑formed abbreviated Data Cubes and that terms are used consistently with their declared semantics.
Users can judge that each dataset has exactly one associated data structure definition.
Users can know that each observation must have a complete set of dimension values and all measure values.
Publishers can know which attachment level (DataSet or Slice) to use for component properties when structuring observations.
Users can know that for datasets with multiple measures, each observation must provide a value for every measure.
Users can know that values of a time dimension may be represented as URIs from a reference time service
Users can know the type of contact point information for a dataset.
Users can know that every qb:Slice must have a value for each dimension declared in its qb:sliceStructure for a Slice.
Users can know that a slice can have an identity URI to enable annotation or external reference.
Users can know which dimension (e.g., sex) is used to define a slice to construct appropriate queries.
Users can know the minimum set of required metadata fields for a DCAT‑compliant catalog.
Users can find the code list associated with a dimension property and verify that each observation's value for that dimension is included in the code list.
Users can know the thematic classification (SKOS concept) of a dataset.
Users can judge that the data structure has not changed across publications.
Users can know the language of a catalog.
Users can know that resources defined by the Library of Congress should be used for controlled vocabularies

Users can know which properties are recommended for use on a dcat:Distribution, such as accessURL, byteSize, description, downloadURL, format, license, mediaType, releaseDate, rights, title, and updateDate.
Users can know the distinction between dcat:Dataset and dcat:CatalogRecord and when to use each.
Users can know that a DCAT catalog must be organized into datasets and distributions and must provide an RDF description of the catalog, its datasets and distributions.
Users can know core metadata of a dataset such as title, description, issued date, modified date, subject.
Users can know how to choose attachment levels for components (attributes) when defining a DataStructureDefinition.
Users can know that the dcat:mediaType property SHOULD be used when the distribution’s type is defined by IANA; otherwise dct:format MAY be used.
Users can find the download URL for a dataset when it is directly available.
Users can know when to use dcat:accessURL versus dcat:downloadURL for a distribution.
All classes and properties defined in DCAT must be used in a way consistent with the semantics declared in this specification.
Users can know that observations are the actual measured values in a statistical data set.
Publishers can optionally annotate a component with a code list to indicate the set of concepts used as codes.
Users can judge whether a DataSet that does not use a Measure dimension provides values for all declared measures in each Observation
Users can know the semantics of date properties such as release date, modification date, and listing date for datasets and catalog records.
Users can know release date (dct:issued) for a Catalog
Users can find the unit of measurement and whether a value is measured or estimated for an Observation.
Users can know that dataset themes are represented by skos:Concepts organized in a skos:ConceptScheme, linked via dcat:themeTaxonomy.
Users can know the title of a Catalog
Users can know that all DCAT classes and properties must be used consistently with the semantics declared in the specification.
Users can know the prefixes and namespaces for the community SDMX resources (sdmx-concept, sdmx-code, sdmx-dimension, sdmx-attribute, sdmx-measure) that may be used in datasets.
Users can know how to query observed values uniformly for a dataset without first parsing the data structure definition, when a normalized representation is used.
Users can know that only attributes may be marked optional in a DataStructureDefinition for a Component.
Users can know that all metadata fields about a catalog, its datasets and distributions are to be included in the RDF description using appropriate DCAT classes and properties.
Publishers can decide at which level (dataset, slice, observation, or measure property) to attach a component property.
Users can know the download URL of a Distribution via dcat:downloadURL.
Users can know that values of a time dimension may be represented using date‑time literals.
Users can know language for a catalog.
Publishers can know when to use a qb:HierarchicalCodeList instead of a SKOS ConceptScheme for representing hierarchical code lists.
Users can know update/modification date (dct:modified) for a Catalog
Users can know the conformance criteria for DCAT that require usage of only terms in the DCAT namespace.
Users can know the spatial coverage of a Dataset via dct:spatial.
Users can know that coded values should be represented as skos:Concepts within a skos:ConceptScheme or skos:Collection
Users can know which attributes are marked as required for qb:Observations.
Users can know the dataset's publisher and SPARQL endpoint for a Dataset.
Users can know when to use code lists versus free text for dimension values, especially when a dimension property has a hierarchical code list.
Users can find slice definitions and their structure to group observations, when they need to discover subsets of a dataset.
Users can know that component properties such as unit of measure can be attached at the dataset level to avoid redundancy.
